article.title: The Secret Spy Network Feeding Russia’s War Machine
Badenoch condemns Reform UK’s ‘authoritarian’ press bans – UK politics live
article.full_text: Q: [From Emilio Casalicchio from Politico] Reform UK have banned seven reporters from their conference, including the one who revealed Nigel Farage got a £5m donation he did not declare. What do you think of that in terms of free speech? And would you do something like that? Badenoch replied: Absolutely not … Conservatives believe in free speech, where people are welcome to criticise us as much as they like. If you look at Nigel Farage’s attacks on the press, some of them very personal … you look at the things that Zia Yusuf says about journalists constantly, you know what kind of government they would be – authoritarian and using state power to pursue opponents. [That is] what they’ve effectively been threatening. We do not do that. It’s absolutely not something that we believe in. We believe in free speech. We believe in a free press. And yes, of course, that might be painful for us as politicians, but public scrutiny is part of the gig. If Nigel Farage can’t handle difficult questions about his dodgy £5m, then he shouldn’t be a politician. But that comes with, working as an MP and standing to be leader of the country. Badenoch has not always been comfortable with press scrutiny herself. As a minister in the last government, she was criticised for her aggressive response to journalists reporting on her. But as Conservative leader she has been more tolerant of criticism, and while the Tories don’t exactly welcome negative press coverage, they are more pro-media than Reform UK. Back to what was said at Kemi Badenoch’s press conference. Q: [From Jonathan Walker from the Express] Are you ready to lead the country into war if necessary? Badenoch replied: If you want a peace, you have to prepare for war. And I believe that strong countries don’t get attacked. It’s countries that look weak that get attacked. And I look at what Poland is doing. Why are they increasing their army to 300,000? Why are they withdrawing from all these treaties that would stop them from fighting a war? I was in Rome last week speaking to Giorgia Meloni about defence. I spoke to Prime Minister Mitsotakis in Greece about defence. Everybody is worried. So why are we pretending that nothing’s happening? That’s what should concern us, that we have a government that’s talking about things that are not to do with national security, just their pet projects and hobby horses. Yes, we all want cheaper bus fares, but if anything happens to a Nato country, so much damage will be done we’re not going to be getting any growth. Emmanuel Macron, the French president, is meeting Andy Burnham in Downing Street. In public remarks at the start of their meeting, Burnham said: I’m very pleased today to welcome my first overseas visitor as prime minister, and it’s so fitting that it is our nearest neighbour and close friend Emmanuel. On behalf of everyone here, Mr Le President, can I thank you for your huge personal gesture of goodwill, trust and friendship with Britain in allowing the Bayeux Tapestry to be displayed here. Burnham said the exhibition would “lift so many lives”. He added: It shows what collaboration can achieve, just as we are also showing on Ukraine, on small boats, and also on strengthening the UK-EU relationship. So I look forward to discussing those themes further with you today. Q: If Diane Abbott was a Tory MP, would you sack her over her tweet saying the threat from Russia is a Nato fiction. In a post on X now removed, Abbott said: The imminent threat from Russia is a Nato fiction to justify their complete capitulation to Trump’s demands for more military spending. The increase should not go ahead. Badenoch said there was “only so much diversity of opinion that I think that we will tolerate”. Being against Nato was not a Conservative position, she said. She went on: So I fundamentally disagree with Diane Abbott. That is the Labour party. That’s the Labour party view. She’s not the only one who thinks that.
